# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1445
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1445
- **Title**: gh-1441 Voxel nodes render as the “Voxel world” placeholder — Fa app builds JsonWidgetRenderer without voxelWorld (fa-craft 0.2.18, voxel-sandbox 1.0.0)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1441` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +703
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T11:45:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T13:01:28Z

## PR Description

Closes #1441
### Root Cause

`voxel` nodes render the "Voxel world" placeholder because the Fa app built `JsonWidgetRenderer` **without `voxelWorld`** at both construction sites — the fullscreen view (`js_app_view.dart` `_treeView`) and the live tile (`dynamic_widget_tile.dart`). The runtime falls back to the `Icons.landscape` placeholder exactly when the world is null, so `fa-craft`/`voxel-sandbox` resolved their `voxel.*` probes and uploaded meshes while the screen showed the placeholder (exposed by the gh-1341 `js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156 pin, which made the widgets' probes resolve).

### Fix

- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`: expose `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _engine?.voxelWorld;` — always the CURRENT engine's bridge-owned world (null before start / after dispose, so a reload re-wires, never a stale world). Plus `noteUnwiredVoxelWorld(tree)`: a one-shot `AppLog` diagnostic so a null world on a voxel tree reads as "host wiring", not "broken widget".
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_view.dart`: pass `voxelWorld: engine.voxelWorld` (mirrors the existing `webViewHost`/`js3dHost` wiring) + the diagnostic call.
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/dynamic_widget_tile.dart`: same wiring in `DynamicWidgetCanvas`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/jsr_voxel_world_pin_guard_test.dart` (REG-1): static guard asserting every `JsonWidgetRenderer(` in both surfaces passes `voxelWorld:` and the getter delegates to `_engine` — **failed before the fix** (reproduction), blocks merge even when widget tests skip.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/js_app_engine_voxel_world_test.dart` (UT-1/AC5+AC3): world identity across restart, null before start/after dispose; one-shot diagnostic asserted via `AppLog.dump()`; null-world placeholder still renders without crash.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/js_app_view_voxel_test.dart` (IT-1/AC1+E1): real-engine boot through `JsAppView` — `JsVoxelNode` present, placeholder absent; bare first-tree voxel node (zero `voxel.*` calls) renders via the eager bridge world.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/dynamic_widget_tile_voxel_test.dart` (IT-2/AC2): same assertions through the tile canvas.
- Engine-dependent legs gated on `quickJsBridgeAvailable` (repo pattern): live-verified on Linux QuickJS (`LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH`), run on the CI macOS exzone leg, skip on bare ubuntu.
- Regression sweep on this runner: `flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps` → **543 passed, 0 failed** (the CI exzone surface, engines live); the diff's importing suites (`test/golden`, `app_launcher_screen_test`, `chat_screen_test`, `analytics_guard_test`) → 41 passed; full `flutter_app` suite failures (222) are byte-identical on the pre-fix baseline commit and confined to the host-locked golden suite (220 — documented ubuntu-excluded in `ci.yml`) plus 2 env-bound legs (wasm shell scripting, OAuth port binding) in suites this diff never touches. `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`: no issues in changed files.

### Notes

- Degradation contract (AC3) kept: a world-less engine still renders the renderer's placeholder; shipped backends always have a world, so the diagnostic never fires there.
- AC4 catalog-app E2E goldens (`fa-craft`, `voxel-sandbox`) are not executable in this runner — the fixtures live in the remote catalog; the IT tests replicate their exact probe → upload → camera protocol instead.
- REG-2 backend parity: the getter is backend-agnostic; the live-world leg covers the native flutter_js backend (QuickJS here, JSC on macOS CI). The web-worker backend is upstream-owned and not loadable in `flutter_test` on this runner.

## Goal — Voxel nodes render their worlds in the Fa app (v1)

One sentence: **every `{type:'voxel'}` node in a JS app rendered by the Fa app draws its bridge-owned voxel world on every Fa surface** — no surface silently swaps the world for a placeholder while the engine side reports success.

Today the opposite: `fa-craft` 0.2.18 and `voxel-sandbox` 1.0.0 upload chunk meshes (the bridge resolves `voxel.attach` / `voxel.mesh` / `voxel.camera`), the apps report "native" / "voxel node live", and the screen shows the renderer's `Icons.landscape` + **"Voxel world" placeholder** — because the Fa app constructs `JsonWidgetRenderer` **without `voxelWorld`** at both of its construction sites.

## Why this framing

- "The voxel apps are broken" is the wrong subject — the widgets are correct, the runtime node is correct; the missing piece is one wiring parameter at two construction sites in **this repo**.
- The bug was **exposed** by the gh-1341 fix (closed #1366): before the `js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156 pin, `jsr.hostCall` promises hung forever on JSC builds, so fa-craft degraded to the legacy `scene3d` software path (slow but **visible**) and voxel-sandbox spun forever. With 0.4.156 the probes now resolve, both apps take the native voxel path — and land on the placeholder. The 1341 fix traded "slow but visible" for "fast but invisible".

## Architecture / root cause (pinned facts)

Runtime (`js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156, pinned at `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml:68`):

- `JsWidgetBridge` owns `final JsVoxelWorld voxelWorld = JsVoxelWorld();` — created **eagerly at engine start**, always non-null (`lib/src/runtime/js_widget_bridge.dart:134`). `voxel.*` host calls are intercepted **before** the host handler (`:357-369`) — which is why `voxel.attach` resolves although this repo has no voxel code at all.
- `JsWidgetEngine` already exposes it: `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _backend.voxelWorld;` (`lib/src/runtime/js_widget_engine_wrapper.dart:77`).
- The renderer node: `'voxel' => _voxel(m)` → `if (voxelWorld == null) return _mediaPlaceholder(m, Icons.landscape, label: 'Voxel world');` else `JsVoxelNode(world: voxelWorld!, …)` (`lib/src/renderer/json_widget_renderer.dart:619-623`). The constructor param doc states the contract: *"Engines expose their bridge-owned world; hosts rendering trees without an engine pass the world they fill."*

Fa app (this repo) — **both** `JsonWidgetRenderer` construction sites omit `voxelWorld`:

- fullscreen: `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_view.dart`, `_treeView` (~:833) — passes `theme` / `mapTileProvider` / `mediaHost` / `webViewHost` / `js3dHost` / `onScene3dTap` / `onEvent`, no `voxelWorld`;
- live tile: `flutter_app/lib/apps/dynamic_widget_tile.dart` (~:376) — `mediaHost` / `js3dHost` / `onScene3dTap` / `onEvent`, no `voxelWorld`;
- the Fa wrapper `JsAppEngine` keeps the runtime engine private (`JsWidgetEngine? _engine`, `js_app_engine.dart:307`; only `exportedState` / `peekLogs` are exposed) — there is no `voxelWorld` accessor either.

**Fix sketch:** add `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _engine?.voxelWorld;` to Fa's `JsAppEngine`, and pass `voxelWorld: engine.voxelWorld` at both renderer sites, mirroring the existing `webViewHost` / `js3dHost` wiring comments ("the SAME host the engine's JsRuntimeConfig got — see JsAppEngine.start").

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1445
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1445
- **Title**: gh-1441 Voxel nodes render as the “Voxel world” placeholder — Fa app builds JsonWidgetRenderer without voxelWorld (fa-craft 0.2.18, voxel-sandbox 1.0.0)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1441` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +703
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T11:45:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T13:01:28Z

## PR Description

Closes #1441
### Root Cause

`voxel` nodes render the "Voxel world" placeholder because the Fa app built `JsonWidgetRenderer` **without `voxelWorld`** at both construction sites — the fullscreen view (`js_app_view.dart` `_treeView`) and the live tile (`dynamic_widget_tile.dart`). The runtime falls back to the `Icons.landscape` placeholder exactly when the world is null, so `fa-craft`/`voxel-sandbox` resolved their `voxel.*` probes and uploaded meshes while the screen showed the placeholder (exposed by the gh-1341 `js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156 pin, which made the widgets' probes resolve).

### Fix

- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`: expose `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _engine?.voxelWorld;` — always the CURRENT engine's bridge-owned world (null before start / after dispose, so a reload re-wires, never a stale world). Plus `noteUnwiredVoxelWorld(tree)`: a one-shot `AppLog` diagnostic so a null world on a voxel tree reads as "host wiring", not "broken widget".
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_view.dart`: pass `voxelWorld: engine.voxelWorld` (mirrors the existing `webViewHost`/`js3dHost` wiring) + the diagnostic call.
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/dynamic_widget_tile.dart`: same wiring in `DynamicWidgetCanvas`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/jsr_voxel_world_pin_guard_test.dart` (REG-1): static guard asserting every `JsonWidgetRenderer(` in both surfaces passes `voxelWorld:` and the getter delegates to `_engine` — **failed before the fix** (reproduction), blocks merge even when widget tests skip.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/js_app_engine_voxel_world_test.dart` (UT-1/AC5+AC3): world identity across restart, null before start/after dispose; one-shot diagnostic asserted via `AppLog.dump()`; null-world placeholder still renders without crash.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/js_app_view_voxel_test.dart` (IT-1/AC1+E1): real-engine boot through `JsAppView` — `JsVoxelNode` present, placeholder absent; bare first-tree voxel node (zero `voxel.*` calls) renders via the eager bridge world.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/dynamic_widget_tile_voxel_test.dart` (IT-2/AC2): same assertions through the tile canvas.
- Engine-dependent legs gated on `quickJsBridgeAvailable` (repo pattern): live-verified on Linux QuickJS (`LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH`), run on the CI macOS exzone leg, skip on bare ubuntu.
- Regression sweep on this runner: `flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps` → **543 passed, 0 failed** (the CI exzone surface, engines live); the diff's importing suites (`test/golden`, `app_launcher_screen_test`, `chat_screen_test`, `analytics_guard_test`) → 41 passed; full `flutter_app` suite failures (222) are byte-identical on the pre-fix baseline commit and confined to the host-locked golden suite (220 — documented ubuntu-excluded in `ci.yml`) plus 2 env-bound legs (wasm shell scripting, OAuth port binding) in suites this diff never touches. `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`: no issues in changed files.

### Notes

- Degradation contract (AC3) kept: a world-less engine still renders the renderer's placeholder; shipped backends always have a world, so the diagnostic never fires there.
- AC4 catalog-app E2E goldens (`fa-craft`, `voxel-sandbox`) are not executable in this runner — the fixtures live in the remote catalog; the IT tests replicate their exact probe → upload → camera protocol instead.

# gh-1441: Voxel nodes render as the “Voxel world” placeholder — Fa app builds JsonWidgetRenderer without voxelWorld (fa-craft 0.2.18, voxel-sandbox 1.0.0)

## Description

## Goal — Voxel nodes render their worlds in the Fa app (v1)

One sentence: **every `{type:'voxel'}` node in a JS app rendered by the Fa app draws its bridge-owned voxel world on every Fa surface** — no surface silently swaps the world for a placeholder while the engine side reports success.

Today the opposite: `fa-craft` 0.2.18 and `voxel-sandbox` 1.0.0 upload chunk meshes (the bridge resolves `voxel.attach` / `voxel.mesh` / `voxel.camera`), the apps report "native" / "voxel node live", and the screen shows the renderer's `Icons.landscape` + **"Voxel world" placeholder** — because the Fa app constructs `JsonWidgetRenderer` **without `voxelWorld`** at both of its construction sites.

## Why this framing

- "The voxel apps are broken" is the wrong subject — the widgets are correct, the runtime node is correct; the missing piece is one wiring parameter at two construction sites in **this repo**.
- The bug was **exposed** by the gh-1341 fix (closed #1366): before the `js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156 pin, `jsr.hostCall` promises hung forever on JSC builds, so fa-craft degraded to the legacy `scene3d` software path (slow but **visible**) and voxel-sandbox spun forever. With 0.4.156 the probes now resolve, both apps take the native voxel path — and land on the placeholder. The 1341 fix traded "slow but visible" for "fast but invisible".

## Architecture / root cause (pinned facts)

Runtime (`js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156, pinned at `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml:68`):

- `JsWidgetBridge` owns `final JsVoxelWorld voxelWorld = JsVoxelWorld();` — created **eagerly at engine start**, always non-null (`lib/src/runtime/js_widget_bridge.dart:134`). `voxel.*` host calls are intercepted **before** the host handler (`:357-369`) — which is why `voxel.attach` resolves although this repo has no voxel code at all.
- `JsWidgetEngine` already exposes it: `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _backend.voxelWorld;` (`lib/src/runtime/js_widget_engine_wrapper.dart:77`).
- The renderer node: `'voxel' => _voxel(m)` → `if (voxelWorld == null) return _mediaPlaceholder(m, Icons.landscape, label: 'Voxel world');` else `JsVoxelNode(world: voxelWorld!, …)` (`lib/src/renderer/json_widget_renderer.dart:619-623`). The constructor param doc states the contract: *"Engines expose their bridge-owned world; hosts rendering trees without an engine pass the world they fill."*

Fa app (this repo) — **both** `JsonWidgetRenderer` construction sites omit `voxelWorld`:

- fullscreen: `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_view.dart`, `_treeView` (~:833) — passes `theme` / `mapTileProvider` / `mediaHost` / `webViewHost` / `js3dHost` / `onScene3dTap` / `onEvent`, no `voxelWorld`;
- live tile: `flutter_app/lib/apps/dynamic_widget_tile.dart` (~:376) — `mediaHost` / `js3dHost` / `onScene3dTap` / `onEvent`, no `voxelWorld`;
- the Fa wrapper `JsAppEngine` keeps the runtime engine private (`JsWidgetEngine? _engine`, `js_app_engine.dart:307`; only `exportedState` / `peekLogs` are exposed) — there is no `voxelWorld` accessor either.

**Fix sketch:** add `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _engine?.voxelWorld;` to Fa's `JsAppEngine`, and pass `voxelWorld: engine.voxelWorld` at both renderer sites, mirroring the existing `webViewHost` / `js3dHost` wiring comments ("the SAME host the engine's JsRuntimeConfig got — see JsAppEngine.start").

## Evidence / reproduction

- Device: Fa iOS app (JavaScriptCore backend), 2026-10-09.
- **fa-craft 0.2.18** (catalog auto-update; `minRuntime 0.4.79`): screen = full-bleed "Voxel world" placeholder under the HUD crosshair. App log (repeated, stable):
  `{id: [facraft] v=0.2.18 fps=120 hud=0.4ms mesh=7.8ms uploads=25 meshKB=2021 native=true}` — the probe resolved, ~2 MB of chunk uploads accepted, per-frame `voxel.camera` flowing; nothing renders.
- **voxel-sandbox 1.0.0** (`minRuntime 0.4.127`): sky-blue 240 px box containing the same placeholder; the status row literally reads **"9 chunks · 1296 faces" / "voxel node live"** — the widget's own support probe resolved, so the banner claims the node is live while the pixels say otherwise.
- No JS errors in `app.log` (`widget eval error` absent); the trees contain a valid `{type:'voxel', id}` node, so the placeholder is the renderer's null-world fallback, not a parse failure.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — For an engine whose tree contains `{type:'voxel'}` after a successful `voxel.attach` + `voxel.mesh`, the fullscreen surface builds a `JsVoxelNode` and NOT the "Voxel world" `_mediaPlaceholder` (hook: widget test rendering the engine tree through the `js_app_view` body, `find.byType(JsVoxelNode)` / golden without the landscape icon).
- **AC2** — The same assertion holds for the live-tile surface (`dynamic_widget_tile.dart`) when a tile tree contains a voxel node (hook: the existing tile test harness).
- **AC3** — Degradation contract intact: on a minimal custom backend where `backend.voxelWorld == null`, the placeholder still renders (no crash) AND a one-line diagnostic is logged so authoring agents can tell "host did not wire voxelWorld" from "broken widget" (hook: fake-backend test asserting the log record).
- **AC4** — The catalog fixtures `fa-craft` and `voxel-sandbox` render actual terrain in this repo's E2E/golden harness (hook: golden snapshots; both apps already exercise probe → upload → camera).
- **AC5** — Reload re-wires the CURRENT world: after `JsAppEngine.reload`/restart, a subsequent render uses the new engine's `voxelWorld` — never a stale world from the disposed engine (hook: test asserting instance identity across reload).

## Test plan

### Test matrix — maximal coverage, zero cross-platform breakage

- `UT-1` (AC5): `JsAppEngine.voxelWorld` returns `_engine.voxelWorld`; `null` before start and after dispose — pure fake backend.
- `IT-1` (AC1, AC3): `js_app_view` widget test with `MemoryExecutionEnv` + fixture widget (probe + one chunk + camera) asserting `JsVoxelNode` presence; null-world fake asserts placeholder + diagnostic log (fakes, deterministic clock).
- `IT-2` (AC2): the same fixture through the tile builder.
- `E2E-1` (AC4): golden render of the voxel-sandbox fixture at engine start and after a `dig` event; parity with the runtime's `test/voxel_sandbox_logic_test.dart` expectations (semantic-drift property: the two repos' goldens must not diverge silently).
- `REG-1` (AC1/AC2): a source pin-guard in the style of `test/jsr_host_call_pin_guard_test.dart` — scan `js_app_view.dart` and `dynamic_widget_tile.dart`, assert every `JsonWidgetRenderer(` construction passes `voxelWorld:`. CI rule: **a red REG job blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**
- `REG-2` (backend parity): for every shipped backend (flutter_js/JSC, web worker) assert `engine.voxelWorld != null` after start, so the wiring cannot silently regress on one platform (negative control: the minimal test backend stays null by design — covered by IT-1's fake).

### Edge / border cases

- **E1** — Voxel node in the FIRST tree, before any `voxel.*` call: the bridge world is eager (`js_widget_bridge.dart:134`), so with wiring the first frame already renders (empty sky) — test asserts no placeholder on a bare `{type:'voxel'}` tree with zero chunks.
- **E2** — Older runtime / rejecting hostCall: the widget's own probe rejects → apps keep their documented graceful paths (voxel-sandbox "voxel node unsupported" banner; fa-craft legacy `scene3d` fallback). Unchanged by this fix — pinned by a fake-backend rejection test.
- **E3** — Two engines live at once (fullscreen + tile of the same app): each renderer must get ITS engine's world; no cross-talk (test: two engines, distinct chunk colors).
- **E4** — Dispose/reload mid-flight: a pending `voxel.mesh` for a disposed engine must not paint into the new world (identity assert in UT-1/AC5).
- **E5** — `jsr.capture` (runtime 0.4.128+) on a voxel tree captures the rendered world, not the placeholder (golden hash differs from the placeholder golden).

## Non-goals

- No GPU/3D-engine rewrite of the voxel pipeline — upstream's "GPU vox…

content.text:
## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`

- **Title**: gh-1441 Voxel nodes render as the “Voxel world” placeholder — Fa app builds JsonWidgetRenderer without voxelWorld (fa-craft 0.2.18, voxel-sandbox 1.0.0)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1441` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +703
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T11:45:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T13:01:28Z

## PR Description

Closes #1441
### Root Cause

`voxel` nodes render the "Voxel world" placeholder because the Fa app built `JsonWidgetRenderer` **without `voxelWorld`** at both construction sites — the fullscreen view (`js_app_view.dart` `_treeView`) and the live tile (`dynamic_widget_tile.dart`). The runtime falls back to the `Icons.landscape` placeholder exactly when the world is null, so `fa-craft`/`voxel-sandbox` resolved their `voxel.*` probes and uploaded meshes while the screen showed the placeholder (exposed by the gh-1341 `js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156 pin, which made the widgets' probes resolve).

### Fix

- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`: expose `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _engine?.voxelWorld;` — always the CURRENT engine's bridge-owned world (null before start / after dispose, so a reload re-wires, never a stale world). Plus `noteUnwiredVoxelWorld(tree)`: a one-shot `AppLog` diagnostic so a null world on a voxel tree reads as "host wiring", not "broken widget".
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_view.dart`: pass `voxelWorld: engine.voxelWorld` (mirrors the existing `webViewHost`/`js3dHost` wiring) + the diagnostic call.
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/dynamic_widget_tile.dart`: same wiring in `DynamicWidgetCanvas`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/jsr_voxel_world_pin_guard_test.dart` (REG-1): static guard asserting every `JsonWidgetRenderer(` in both surfaces passes `voxelWorld:` and the getter delegates to `_engine` — **failed before the fix** (reproduction), blocks merge even when widget tests skip.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/js_app_engine_voxel_world_test.dart` (UT-1/AC5+AC3): world identity across restart, null before start/after dispose; one-shot diagnostic asserted via `AppLog.dump()`; null-world placeholder still renders without crash.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/js_app_view_voxel_test.dart` (IT-1/AC1+E1): real-engine boot through `JsAppView` — `JsVoxelNode` present, placeholder absent; bare first-tree voxel node (zero `voxel.*` calls) renders via the eager bridge world.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/dynamic_widget_tile_voxel_test.dart` (IT-2/AC2): same assertions through the tile canvas.
- Engine-dependent legs gated on `quickJsBridgeAvailable` (repo pattern): live-verified on Linux QuickJS (`LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH`), run on the CI macOS exzone leg, skip on bare ubuntu.
- Regression sweep on this runner: `flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps` → **543 passed, 0 failed** (the CI exzone surface, engines live); the diff's importing suites (`test/golden`, `app_launcher_screen_test`, `chat_screen_test`, `analytics_guard_test`) → 41 passed; full `flutter_app` suite failures (222) are byte-identical on the pre-fix baseline commit and confined to the host-locked golden suite (220 — documented ubuntu-excluded in `ci.yml`) plus 2 env-bound legs (wasm shell scripting, OAuth port binding) in suites this diff never touches. `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`: no issues in changed files.

### Notes

- Degradation contract (AC3) kept: a world-less engine still renders the renderer's placeholder; shipped backends always have a world, so the diagnostic never fires there.
- AC4 catalog-app E2E goldens (`fa-craft`, `voxel-sandbox`) are not executable in this runner — the fixtures live in the remote catalog; the IT tests replicate their exact probe → upload → camera protocol instead.
- REG-2 backend parity: the getter is backend-agnostic; the live-world leg covers the native flutter_js backend (QuickJS here, JSC on macOS CI). The web-worker backend is upstream-owned and not loadable in `flutter_test` on this runner.

blocks.text:
# gh-1441: Voxel nodes render as the “Voxel world” placeholder — Fa app builds JsonWidgetRenderer without voxelWorld (fa-craft 0.2.18, voxel-sandbox 1.0.0)

## Description

## Goal — Voxel nodes render their worlds in the Fa app (v1)

One sentence: **every `{type:'voxel'}` node in a JS app rendered by the Fa app draws its bridge-owned voxel world on every Fa surface** — no surface silently swaps the world for a placeholder while the engine side reports success.

Today the opposite: `fa-craft` 0.2.18 and `voxel-sandbox` 1.0.0 upload chunk meshes (the bridge resolves `voxel.attach` / `voxel.mesh` / `voxel.camera`), the apps report "native" / "voxel node live", and the screen shows the renderer's `Icons.landscape` + **"Voxel world" placeholder** — because the Fa app constructs `JsonWidgetRenderer` **without `voxelWorld`** at both of its construction sites.

## Why this framing

- "The voxel apps are broken" is the wrong subject — the widgets are correct, the runtime node is correct; the missing piece is one wiring parameter at two construction sites in **this repo**.
- The bug was **exposed** by the gh-1341 fix (closed #1366): before the `js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156 pin, `jsr.hostCall` promises hung forever on JSC builds, so fa-craft degraded to the legacy `scene3d` software path (slow but **visible**) and voxel-sandbox spun forever. With 0.4.156 the probes now resolve, both apps take the native voxel path — and land on the placeholder. The 1341 fix traded "slow but visible" for "fast but invisible".

## Architecture / root cause (pinned facts)

Runtime (`js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156, pinned at `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml:68`):

- `JsWidgetBridge` owns `final JsVoxelWorld voxelWorld = JsVoxelWorld();` — created **eagerly at engine start**, always non-null (`lib/src/runtime/js_widget_bridge.dart:134`). `voxel.*` host calls are intercepted **before** the host handler (`:357-369`) — which is why `voxel.attach` resolves although this repo has no voxel code at all.
- `JsWidgetEngine` already exposes it: `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _backend.voxelWorld;` (`lib/src/runtime/js_widget_engine_wrapper.dart:77`).
- The renderer node: `'voxel' => _voxel(m)` → `if (voxelWorld == null) return _mediaPlaceholder(m, Icons.landscape, label: 'Voxel world');` else `JsVoxelNode(world: voxelWorld!, …)` (`lib/src/renderer/json_widget_renderer.dart:619-623`). The constructor param doc states the contract: *"Engines expose their bridge-owned world; hosts rendering trees without an engine pass the world they fill."*

Fa app (this repo) — **both** `JsonWidgetRenderer` construction sites omit `voxelWorld`:

- fullscreen: `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_view.dart`, `_treeView` (~:833) — passes `theme` / `mapTileProvider` / `mediaHost` / `webViewHost` / `js3dHost` / `onScene3dTap` / `onEvent`, no `voxelWorld`;
- live tile: `flutter_app/lib/apps/dynamic_widget_tile.dart` (~:376) — `mediaHost` / `js3dHost` / `onScene3dTap` / `onEvent`, no `voxelWorld`;
- the Fa wrapper `JsAppEngine` keeps the runtime engine private (`JsWidgetEngine? _engine`, `js_app_engine.dart:307`; only `exportedState` / `peekLogs` are exposed) — there is no `voxelWorld` accessor either.

**Fix sketch:** add `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _engine?.voxelWorld;` to Fa's `JsAppEngine`, and pass `voxelWorld: engine.voxelWorld` at both renderer sites, mirroring the existing `webViewHost` / `js3dHost` wiring comments ("the SAME host the engine's JsRuntimeConfig got — see JsAppEngine.start").

## Evidence / reproduction

- Device: Fa iOS app (JavaScriptCore backend), 2026-10-09.
- **fa-craft 0.2.18** (catalog auto-update; `minRuntime 0.4.79`): screen = full-bleed "Voxel world" placeholder under the HUD crosshair. App log (repeated, stable):
  `{id: [facraft] v=0.2.18 fps=120 hud=0.4ms mesh=7.8ms uploads=25 meshKB=2021 native=true}` — the probe resolved, ~2 MB of chunk uploads accepted, per-frame `voxel.camera` flowing; nothing renders.
- **voxel-sandbox 1.0.0** (`minRuntime 0.4.127`): sky-blue 240 px box containing the same placeholder; the status row literally reads **"9 chunks · 1296 faces" / "voxel node live"** — the widget's own support probe resolved, so the banner claims the node is live while the pixels say otherwise.
- No JS errors in `app.log` (`widget eval error` absent); the trees contain a valid `{type:'voxel', id}` node, so the placeholder is the renderer's null-world fallback, not a parse failure.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — For an engine whose tree contains `{type:'voxel'}` after a successful `voxel.attach` + `voxel.mesh`, the fullscreen surface builds a `JsVoxelNode` and NOT the "Voxel world" `_mediaPlaceholder` (hook: widget test rendering the engine tree through the `js_app_view` body, `find.byType(JsVoxelNode)` / golden without the landscape icon).
- **AC2** — The same assertion holds for the live-tile surface (`dynamic_widget_tile.dart`) when a tile tree contains a voxel node (hook: the existing tile test harness).
- **AC3** — Degradation contract intact: on a minimal custom backend where `backend.voxelWorld == null`, the placeholder still renders (no crash) AND a one-line diagnostic is logged so authoring agents can tell "host did not wire voxelWorld" from "broken widget" (hook: fake-backend test asserting the log record).
- **AC4** — The catalog fixtures `fa-craft` and `voxel-sandbox` render actual terrain in this repo's E2E/golden harness (hook: golden snapshots; both apps already exercise probe → upload → camera).
- **AC5** — Reload re-wires the CURRENT world: after `JsAppEngine.reload`/restart, a subsequent render uses the new engine's `voxelWorld` — never a stale world from the disposed engine (hook: test asserting instance identity across reload).

## Test plan

### Test matrix — maximal coverage, zero cross-platform breakage

- `UT-1` (AC5): `JsAppEngine.voxelWorld` returns `_engine.voxelWorld`; `null` before start and after dispose — pure fake backend.
- `IT-1` (AC1, AC3): `js_app_view` widget test with `MemoryExecutionEnv` + fixture widget (probe + one chunk + camera) asserting `JsVoxelNode` presence; null-world fake asserts placeholder + diagnostic log (fakes, deterministic clock).
- `IT-2` (AC2): the same fixture through the tile builder.
- `E2E-1` (AC4): golden render of the voxel-sandbox fixture at engine start and after a `dig` event; parity with the runtime's `test/voxel_sandbox_logic_test.dart` expectations (semantic-drift property: the two repos' goldens must not diverge silently).
- `REG-1` (AC1/AC2): a source pin-guard in the style of `test/jsr_host_call_pin_guard_test.dart` — scan `js_app_view.dart` and `dynamic_widget_tile.dart`, assert every `JsonWidgetRenderer(` construction passes `voxelWorld:`. CI rule: **a red REG job blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**
- `REG-2` (backend parity): for every shipped backend (flutter_js/JSC, web worker) assert `engine.voxelWorld != null` after start, so the wiring cannot silently regress on one platform (negative control: the minimal test backend stays null by design — covered by IT-1's fake).

### Edge / border cases

- **E1** — Voxel node in the FIRST tree, before any `voxel.*` call: the bridge world is eager (`js_widget_bridge.dart:134`), so with wiring the first frame already renders (empty sky) — test asserts no placeholder on a bare `{type:'voxel'}` tree with zero chunks.
- **E2** — Older runtime / rejecting hostCall: the widget's own probe rejects → apps keep their documented graceful paths (voxel-sandbox "voxel node unsupported" banner; fa-craft legacy `scene3d` fallback). Unchanged by this fix — pinned by a fake-backend rejection test.
- **E3** — Two engines live at once (fullscreen + tile of the same app): each renderer must get ITS engine's world; no cross-talk (test: two engines, distinct chunk colors).
- **E4** — Dispose/reload mid-flight: a pending `voxel.mesh` for a disposed engine must not paint into the new world (identity assert in UT-1/AC5).
- **E5** — `jsr.capture` (runtime 0.4.128+) on a voxel tree captures the rendered world, not the placeholder (golden hash differs from the placeholder golden).

## Non-goals

- No GPU/3D-engine rewrite of the voxel pipeline — upstream's "GPU vox…

blocks.text:
## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - name: flutter test test/apps (JS engine live)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps

  # Issue #433: flutter_app CRAP ratchet — the app's beasts were never

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [changes, flutter-tests]

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## PR Description

Closes #1441
### Root Cause

`voxel` nodes render the "Voxel world" placeholder because the Fa app built `JsonWidgetRenderer` **without `voxelWorld`** at both construction sites — the fullscreen view (`js_app_view.dart` `_treeView`) and the live tile (`dynamic_widget_tile.dart`). - `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`: expose `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _engine?.voxelWorld;` — always the CURRENT engine's bridge-owned world (null before start / after dispose, so a reload re-wires, never a stale world). - `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_view.dart`: pass `voxelWorld: engine.voxelWorld` (mirrors the existing `webViewHost`/`js3dHost` wiring) + the diagnostic call.
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/dynamic_widget_tile.dart`: same wiring in `DynamicWidgetCanvas`.

- `flutter_app/test/apps/dynamic_widget_tile_voxel_test.dart` (IT-2/AC2): same assertions through the tile canvas.

# gh-1441: Voxel nodes render as the “Voxel world” placeholder — Fa app builds JsonWidgetRenderer without voxelWorld (fa-craft 0.2.18, voxel-sandbox 1.0.0)

## Description

## Goal — Voxel nodes render their worlds in the Fa app (v1)

One sentence: **every `{type:'voxel'}` node in a JS app rendered by the Fa app draws its bridge-owned voxel world on every Fa surface** — no surface silently swaps the world for a placeholder while the engine side reports success.

Today the opposite: `fa-craft` 0.2.18 and `voxel-sandbox` 1.0.0 upload chunk meshes (the bridge resolves `voxel.attach` / `voxel.mesh` / `voxel.camera`), the apps report "native" / "voxel node live", and the screen shows the renderer's `Icons.landscape` + **"Voxel world" placeholder** — because the Fa app constructs `JsonWidgetRenderer` **without `voxelWorld`** at both of its construction sites.

## Why this framing

- "The voxel apps are broken" is the wrong subject — the widgets are correct, the runtime node is correct; the missing piece is one wiring parameter at two construction sites in **this repo**.
- The bug was **exposed** by the gh-1341 fix (closed #1366): before the `js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156 pin, `jsr.hostCall` promises hung forever on JSC builds, so fa-craft degraded to the legacy `scene3d` software path (slow but **visible**) and voxel-sandbox spun forever. With 0.4.156 the probes now resolve, both apps take the native voxel path — and land on the placeholder. The 1341 fix traded "slow but visible" for "fast but invisible".

## Architecture / root cause (pinned facts)

Runtime (`js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156, pinned at `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml:68`):

- `JsWidgetBridge` owns `final JsVoxelWorld voxelWorld = JsVoxelWorld();` — created **eagerly at engine start**, always non-null (`lib/src/runtime/js_widget_bridge.dart:134`). `voxel.*` host calls are intercepted **before** the host handler (`:357-369`) — which is why `voxel.attach` resolves although this repo has no voxel code at all.
- `JsWidgetEngine` already exposes it: `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _backend.voxelWorld;` (`lib/src/runtime/js_widget_engine_wrapper.dart:77`).
- The renderer node: `'voxel' => _voxel(m)` → `if (voxelWorld == null) return _mediaPlaceholder(m, Icons.landscape, label: 'Voxel world');` else `JsVoxelNode(world: voxelWorld!, …)` (`lib/src/renderer/json_widget_renderer.dart:619-623`). The constructor param doc states the contract: *"Engines expose their bridge-owned world; hosts rendering trees without an engine pass the world they fill."*

Fa app (this repo) — **both** `JsonWidgetRenderer` construction sites omit `voxelWorld`:

- fullscreen: `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_view.dart`, `_treeView` (~:833) — passes `theme` / `mapTileProvider` / `mediaHost` / `webViewHost` / `js3dHost` / `onScene3dTap` / `onEvent`, no `voxelWorld`;
- live tile: `flutter_app/lib/apps/dynamic_widget_tile.dart` (~:376) — `mediaHost` / `js3dHost` / `onScene3dTap` / `onEvent`, no `voxelWorld`;
- the Fa wrapper `JsAppEngine` keeps the runtime engine private (`JsWidgetEngine? _engine`, `js_app_engine.dart:307`; only `exportedState` / `peekLogs` are exposed) — there is no `voxelWorld` accessor either.

**Fix sketch:** add `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _engine?.voxelWorld;` to Fa's `JsAppEngine`, and pass `voxelWorld: engine.voxelWorld` at both renderer sites, mirroring the existing `webViewHost` / `js3dHost` wiring comments ("the SAME host the engine's JsRuntimeConfig got — see JsAppEngine.start").

## Evidence / reproduction

- Device: Fa iOS app (JavaScriptCore backend), 2026-10-09.
- **fa-craft 0.2.18** (catalog auto-update; `minRuntime 0.4.79`): screen = full-bleed "Voxel world" placeholder under the HUD crosshair. App log (repeated, stable):
  `{id: [facraft] v=0.2.18 fps=120 hud=0.4ms mesh=7.8ms uploads=25 meshKB=2021 native=true}` — the probe resolved, ~2 MB of chunk uploads accepted, per-frame `voxel.camera` flowing; nothing renders.
- **voxel-sandbox 1.0.0** (`minRuntime 0.4.127`): sky-blue 240 px box containing the same placeholder; the status row literally reads **"9 chunks · 1296 faces" / "voxel node live"** — the widget's own support probe resolved, so the banner claims the node is live while the pixels say otherwise.
- No JS errors in `app.log` (`widget eval error` absent); the trees contain a valid `{type:'voxel', id}` node, so the placeholder is the renderer's null-world fallback, not a parse failure.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — For an engine whose tree contains `{type:'voxel'}` after a successful `voxel.attach` + `voxel.mesh`, the fullscreen surface builds a `JsVoxelNode` and NOT the "Voxel world" `_mediaPlaceholder` (hook: widget test rendering the engine tree through the `js_app_view` body, `find.byType(JsVoxelNode)` / golden without the landscape icon).
- **AC2** — The same assertion holds for the live-tile surface (`dynamic_widget_tile.dart`) when a tile tree contains a voxel node (hook: the existing tile test harness).
- **AC3** — Degradation contract intact: on a minimal custom backend where `backend.voxelWorld == null`, the placeholder still renders (no crash) AND a one-line diagnostic is logged so authoring agents can tell "host did not wire voxelWorld" from "broken widget" (hook: fake-backend test asserting the log record).
- **AC4** — The catalog fixtures `fa-craft` and `voxel-sandbox` render actual terrain in this repo's E2E/golden harness (hook: golden snapshots; both apps already exercise probe → upload → camera).
- **AC5** — Reload re-wires the CURRENT world: after `JsAppEngine.reload`/restart, a subsequent render uses the new engine's `voxelWorld` — never a stale world from the disposed engine (hook: test asserting instance identity across reload).

## Test plan

### Test matrix — maximal coverage, zero cross-platform breakage

- `UT-1` (AC5): `JsAppEngine.voxelWorld` returns `_engine.voxelWorld`; `null` before start and after dispose — pure fake backend.
- `IT-1` (AC1, AC3): `js_app_view` widget test with `MemoryExecutionEnv` + fixture widget (probe + one chunk + camera) asserting `JsVoxelNode` presence; null-world fake asserts placeholder + diagnostic log (fakes, deterministic clock).
- `IT-2` (AC2): the same fixture through the tile builder.
- `E2E-1` (AC4): golden render of the voxel-sandbox fixture at engine start and after a `dig` event; parity with the runtime's `test/voxel_sandbox_logic_test.dart` expectations (semantic-drift property: the two repos' goldens must not diverge silently).
- `REG-1` (AC1/AC2): a source pin-guard in the style of `test/jsr_host_call_pin_guard_test.dart` — scan `js_app_view.dart` and `dynamic_widget_tile.dart`, assert every `JsonWidgetRenderer(` construction passes `voxelWorld:`. CI rule: **a red REG job blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**
- `REG-2` (backend parity): for every shipped backend (flutter_js/JSC, web worker) assert `engine.voxelWorld != null` after start, so the wiring cannot silently regress on one platform (negative control: the minimal test backend stays null by design — covered by IT-1's fake).

### Edge / border cases

- **E1** — Voxel node in the FIRST tree, before any `voxel.*` call: the bridge world is eager (`js_widget_bridge.dart:134`), so with wiring the first frame already renders (empty sky) — test asserts no placeholder on a bare `{type:'voxel'}` tree with zero chunks.
- **E2** — Older runtime / rejecting hostCall: the widget's own probe rejects → apps keep their documented graceful paths (voxel-sandbox "voxel node unsupported" banner; fa-craft legacy `scene3d` fallback). Unchanged by this fix — pinned by a fake-backend rejection test.
- **E3** — Two engines live at once (fullscreen + tile of the same app): each renderer must get ITS engine's world; no cross-talk (test: two engines, distinct chunk colors).
- **E4** — Dispose/reload mid-flight: a pending `voxel.mesh` for a disposed engine must not paint into the new world (identity assert in UT-1/AC5).
- **E5** — `jsr.capture` (runtime 0.4.128+) on a voxel tree captures the rendered world, not the placeholder (golden hash differs from the placeholder golden).

## Non-goals

- No GPU/3D-engine rewrite of the voxel pipeline — upstream's "GPU vox…

The renderer is constructed with `voxelWorld: engine.voxelWorld` at build time — fine. But there's a subtle issue: during `start()` restart (`_start`), `_engine` is set to null and a new engine is created. If a rebuild happens between dispose of old engine and assignment of new engine, `voxelWorld` would be null and the placeholder would render, plus `noteUnwiredVoxelWorld` would fire a warning diagnostic — a false-positive log on shipped backends during reload. Actually, `noteUnwiredVoxelWorld` is one-shot per engine instance (the JsAppEngine instance persists across restarts!). Note: `_unwiredVoxelNoted` is an instance field of `JsAppEngine`, and `start()` (restart) reuses the same `JsAppEngine` instance with a NEW `JsWidgetEngine`. So the one-shot flag persists across restarts. That means: if the diagnostic fires once (e.g., during a reload gap where `_engine` is briefly null), it will never fire again for that `JsAppEngine` instance even if a real null-world problem appears later. Conversely, it's fine because the diagnostic is meant to be once-per-engine-instance.

Wait, actually the docs say "Logs ONCE per engine instance". During a reload, the same `JsAppEngine` instance is reused (start() → _start() disposes old _engine, creates new). So if the diagnostic fired during a transient null (e.g., a rebuild during the reload gap when `_engine == null`), it would be permanently "spent" — the real null-world condition later (a minimal backend) would never be reported. Also more importantly: **during a reload, a rebuild while `_engine` is null would pass `voxelWorld: null` to the renderer AND fire the diagnostic** — a false positive "host wiring" warning on shipped backends. How likely is a rebuild during the gap? In `_start()`, `_engine = null` happens synchronously at the beginning; then `await old.dispose()` yields the event loop. ## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`

## PR Description

Closes #1441
### Root Cause

`voxel` nodes render the "Voxel world" placeholder because the Fa app built `JsonWidgetRenderer` **without `voxelWorld`** at both construction sites — the fullscreen view (`js_app_view.dart` `_treeView`) and the live tile (`dynamic_widget_tile.dart`). The runtime falls back to the `Icons.landscape` placeholder exactly when the world is null, so `fa-craft`/`voxel-sandbox` resolved their `voxel.*` probes and uploaded meshes while the screen showed the placeholder (exposed by the gh-1341 `js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156 pin, which made the widgets' probes resolve).

### Fix

- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`: expose `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _engine?.voxelWorld;` — always the CURRENT engine's bridge-owned world (null before start / after dispose, so a reload re-wires, never a stale world). Plus `noteUnwiredVoxelWorld(tree)`: a one-shot `AppLog` diagnostic so a null world on a voxel tree reads as "host wiring", not "broken widget".
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_view.dart`: pass `voxelWorld: engine.voxelWorld` (mirrors the existing `webViewHost`/`js3dHost` wiring) + the diagnostic call.
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/dynamic_widget_tile.dart`: same wiring in `DynamicWidgetCanvas`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/jsr_voxel_world_pin_guard_test.dart` (REG-1): static guard asserting every `JsonWidgetRenderer(` in both surfaces passes `voxelWorld:` and the getter delegates to `_engine` — **failed before the fix** (reproduction), blocks merge even when widget tests skip.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/js_app_engine_voxel_world_test.dart` (UT-1/AC5+AC3): world identity across restart, null before start/after dispose; one-shot diagnostic asserted via `AppLog.dump()`; null-world placeholder still renders without crash.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/js_app_view_voxel_test.dart` (IT-1/AC1+E1): real-engine boot through `JsAppView` — `JsVoxelNode` present, placeholder absent; bare first-tree voxel node (zero `voxel.*` calls) renders via the eager bridge world.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/dynamic_widget_tile_voxel_test.dart` (IT-2/AC2): same assertions through the tile canvas.
- Engine-dependent legs gated on `quickJsBridgeAvailable` (repo pattern): live-verified on Linux QuickJS (`LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH`), run on the CI macOS exzone leg, skip on bare ubuntu.
- Regression sweep on this runner: `flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps` → **543 passed, 0 failed** (the CI exzone surface, engines live); the diff's importing suites (`test/golden`, `app_launcher_screen_test`, `chat_screen_test`, `analytics_guard_test`) → 41 passed; full `flutter_app` suite failures (222) are byte-identical on the pre-fix baseline commit and confined to the host-locked golden suite (220 — documented ubuntu-excluded in `ci.yml`) plus 2 env-bound legs (wasm shell scripting, OAuth port binding) in suites this diff never touches. `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`: no issues in changed files.

### Notes

- Degradation contract (AC3) kept: a world-less engine still renders the renderer's placeholder; shipped backends always have a world, so the diagnostic never fires there.
- AC4 catalog-app E2E goldens (`fa-craft`, `voxel-sandbox`) are not executable in this runner — the fixtures live in the remote catalog; the IT tests replicate their exact probe → upload → camera protocol instead.
- REG-2 backend parity: the getter is backend-agnostic; the live-world leg covers the native flutter_js backend (QuickJS here, JSC on macOS CI). The web-worker backend is upstream-owned and not loadable in `flutter_test` on this runner.

# gh-1441: Voxel nodes render as the “Voxel world” placeholder — Fa app builds JsonWidgetRenderer without voxelWorld (fa-craft 0.2.18, voxel-sandbox 1.0.0)

## Description

## Goal — Voxel nodes render their worlds in the Fa app (v1)

One sentence: **every `{type:'voxel'}` node in a JS app rendered by the Fa app draws its bridge-owned voxel world on every Fa surface** — no surface silently swaps the world for a placeholder while the engine side reports success.

Today the opposite: `fa-craft` 0.2.18 and `voxel-sandbox` 1.0.0 upload chunk meshes (the bridge resolves `voxel.attach` / `voxel.mesh` / `voxel.camera`), the apps report "native" / "voxel node live", and the screen shows the renderer's `Icons.landscape` + **"Voxel world" placeholder** — because the Fa app constructs `JsonWidgetRenderer` **without `voxelWorld`** at both of its construction sites.

## Why this framing

- "The voxel apps are broken" is the wrong subject — the widgets are correct, the runtime node is correct; the missing piece is one wiring parameter at two construction sites in **this repo**.
- The bug was **exposed** by the gh-1341 fix (closed #1366): before the `js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156 pin, `jsr.hostCall` promises hung forever on JSC builds, so fa-craft degraded to the legacy `scene3d` software path (slow but **visible**) and voxel-sandbox spun forever. With 0.4.156 the probes now resolve, both apps take the native voxel path — and land on the placeholder. The 1341 fix traded "slow but visible" for "fast but invisible".

## Architecture / root cause (pinned facts)

Runtime (`js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156, pinned at `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml:68`):

- `JsWidgetBridge` owns `final JsVoxelWorld voxelWorld = JsVoxelWorld();` — created **eagerly at engine start**, always non-null (`lib/src/runtime/js_widget_bridge.dart:134`). `voxel.*` host calls are intercepted **before** the host handler (`:357-369`) — which is why `voxel.attach` resolves although this repo has no voxel code at all.
- `JsWidgetEngine` already exposes it: `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _backend.voxelWorld;` (`lib/src/runtime/js_widget_engine_wrapper.dart:77`).

blocks.text:
## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`

Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Read input context:

BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1445
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1445
- **Title**: gh-1441 Voxel nodes render as the “Voxel world” placeholder — Fa app builds JsonWidgetRenderer without voxelWorld (fa-craft 0.2.18, voxel-sandbox 1.0.0)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1441` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +703
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T11:45:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T13:01:28Z

## PR Description

Closes #1441
### Root Cause

`voxel` nodes render the "Voxel world" placeholder because the Fa app built `JsonWidgetRenderer` **without `voxelWorld`** at both construction sites — the fullscreen view (`js_app_view.dart` `_treeView`) and the live tile (`dynamic_widget_tile.dart`). The runtime falls back to the `Icons.landscape` placeholder exactly when the world is null, so `fa-craft`/`voxel-sandbox` resolved their `voxel.*` probes and uploaded meshes while the screen showed the placeholder (exposed by the gh-1341 `js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156 pin, which made the widgets' probes resolve).

### Fix

- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`: expose `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _engine?.voxelWorld;` — always the CURRENT engine's bridge-owned world (null before start / after dispose, so a reload re-wires, never a stale world). Plus `noteUnwiredVoxelWorld(tree)`: a one-shot `AppLog` diagnostic so a null world on a voxel tree reads as "host wiring", not "broken widget".
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_view.dart`: pass `voxelWorld: engine.voxelWorld` (mirrors the existing `webViewHost`/`js3dHost` wiring) + the diagnostic call.
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/dynamic_widget_tile.dart`: same wiring in `DynamicWidgetCanvas`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/jsr_voxel_world_pin_guard_test.dart` (REG-1): static guard asserting every `JsonWidgetRenderer(` in both surfaces passes `voxelWorld:` and the getter delegates to `_engine` — **failed before the fix** (reproduction), blocks merge even when widget tests skip.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/js_app_engine_voxel_world_test.dart` (UT-1/AC5+AC3): world identity across restart, null before start/after dispose; one-shot diagnostic asserted via `AppLog.dump()`; null-world placeholder still renders without crash.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/js_app_view_voxel_test.dart` (IT-1/AC1+E1): real-engine boot through `JsAppView` — `JsVoxelNode` present, placeholder absent; bare first-tree voxel node (zero `voxel.*` calls) renders via the eager bridge world.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/dynamic_widget_tile_voxel_test.dart` (IT-2/AC2): same assertions through the tile canvas.
- Engine-dependent legs gated on `quickJsBridgeAvailable` (repo pattern): live-verified on Linux QuickJS (`LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH`), run on the CI macOS exzone leg, skip on bare ubuntu.
- Regression sweep on this runner: `flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps` → **543 passed, 0 failed** (the CI exzone surface, engines live); the diff's importing suites (`test/golden`, `app_launcher_screen_test`, `chat_screen_test`, `analytics_guard_test`) → 41 passed; full `flutter_app` suite failures (222) are byte-identical on the pre-fix baseline commit and confined to the host-locked golden suite (220 — documented ubuntu-excluded in `ci.yml`) plus 2 env-bound legs (wasm shell scripting, OAuth port binding) in suites this diff never touches. `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`: no issues in changed files.

### Notes

- Degradation contract (AC3) kept: a world-less engine still renders the renderer's placeholder; shipped backends always have a world, so the diagnostic never fires there.
- AC4 catalog-app E2E goldens (`fa-craft`, `voxel-sandbox`) are not executable in this runner — the fixtures live in the remote catalog; the IT tests replicate their exact probe → upload → camera protocol instead.
- REG-2 backend parity: the getter is backend-agnostic; the live-world leg covers the native flutter_js backend (QuickJS here, JSC on macOS CI). The web-worker backend is upstream-owned and not loadable in `flutter_test` on this runner.
